dead.diagnosis: The server shows no real activity. The member count is irrelevant next to the total lack of interaction.
dead.insight: You don't need more users. You need baseline activity. Bringing people into a dead server lowers quality.
dead.action_reason: Without an active core, every other action is useless. The first step is a minimum critical mass.
dead.activity: Almost no activity. Without intervention there is no sign of recovery.

critical.diagnosis: The server has members but almost no activity. The risk of gradually losing users is high if nothing is done soon.
critical.insight: All useful work right now is re-engaging existing users, not attracting new ones.
critical.action_reason: An event with 5–10 people builds the first core. More effective than open events without an audience.
critical.activity: Very low activity, vulnerable to collapse.

early_stage.diagnosis: The server is in its early stages. There is little data for reliable projections, but current behaviour will set the direction.
early_stage.insight: With little data, any projection is an estimate. What matters now is building the first active core.
early_stage.action_reason: Consistency matters more than scale at this stage. One channel active every day beats one big event.
early_stage.activity: Irregular activity, no established pattern yet.

declining.diagnosis: The server shows a negative trend in both growth and activity. Without intervention, the decline will continue.
declining.insight: The likely cause is not a lack of users — it's the loss of the active core. That's where the problem is.
declining.action_title: Identify and contact formerly active users
declining.action_reason: Winning back a user who already trusted the server is more efficient than attracting a new one.
declining.activity: Activity going down — likely to keep falling.

growing.diagnosis: The server is growing consistently. Now is the time to strengthen the community and improve retention.
growing.insight: Growth is real, but without solid retention it will be lost. Take care of the new-member experience.
growing.action_reason: Growth without retention is loss in disguise. Every new user should see the value within 24 hours.
growing.activity: Activity rising — expect a progressive increase.

stable.diagnosis: The server is stable. There are no clear signs of growth or decline.
stable.insight: Stability can be a trap: without active effort it tends towards gradual decline.
stable.action_reason: Stability needs a push to activate passive users without breaking what already works.
stable.activity: Consistent activity within the usual range.

dead.dominant: Structural stagnation. Without real activity, the server stays as it is or loses inactive members.
dead.alternative_condition: Only if an external action is taken (campaign, event, direct contact with users)
dead.risk: Degradation. Inactive users start leaving, emptying the server.

critical.dominant: Risky stagnation. Minimal activity that could collapse at any distraction.
critical.alternative_condition: If a central active group of 5–10 people is created in the next 2 weeks
critical.risk: Accelerated loss of users who see the server as dead.

early_stage.dominant: Uncertainty. With little data, the server could go either way.
early_stage.alternative_condition: If a community of returning users forms in the first month
early_stage.risk: Early death. The server never develops its own identity.

declining.dominant: Continued decline. The negative trend carries on without intervention.
declining.alternative_condition: If formerly active users are identified and contacted
declining.risk: Collapse. Mass departure of users who perceive the server as dying.

growing.dominant: Sustained growth based on the current trend.
growing.alternative: Stabilisation or plateau. Growth slows as the current acquisition channel runs out.
growing.risk: Reversal. A negative event or missing onboarding reverses the trend.

stable.alternative_condition: If an engagement or gamification action is introduced
stable.risk: Gradual decline. Stability without a push tends to slowly drop.
